extracted.intended_audience: community water systems, water system operators, and regulatory compliance staff (state primacy agencies and EPA regional staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and content/ delivery requirements for Consumer Confidence Reports (CCR) under 40 CFR part 141, including distribution timing, summary content, accommodations, record retention, required updates, and references to regulated contaminant information in Appendix A. Applicable to community water systems and state/tribal primacy agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide CCR to primacy agency and certify distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the date the system is required to distribute the report to its customers, each community water system must provide a copy of the report to the primacy agency and a certification that the report(s) has/have been distributed to customers, and that the information is correct and consistent with the compliance monitoring data previously submitted to the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification must affirm distribution to customers and consistency with previously submitted compliance monitoring data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver report to other agencies/clearinghouses as identified
rubrics_metrics.description: No later than the date the system is required to distribute the report to its customers, each community water system must deliver the report to any other agency or clearinghouse identified by the primacy agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must comply with any additional delivery destinations specified by the primacy agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make reports available to the public upon request and provide accessible formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system must make its reports available to the public upon request. Systems should make a reasonable effort to provide the reports in an accessible format to anyone who requests an accommodation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonable efforts expected to accommodate accessibility needs (e.g., large print, translated, audio) when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post current year's report online for large systems (>=50,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system serving 50,000 or more persons must post its current year's report to a publicly-accessible site on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicly-accessible internet posting is mandatory for systems of this size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of mailing requirement for small systems by Governor/Tribal Leader
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor of a State or their designee, or the Tribal Leader where the Tribe has met eligibility requirements, can waive the mailing requirement for community water systems serving fewer than 10,000 persons. In certain Indian country areas the Regional Administrator may waive the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver applies to the mailing requirement (paragraph (a)); consultation with tribal government is required where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative publication and notice actions for waived systems (<10,000)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems granted the mailing-waiver must (i) publish the reports in one or more local newspapers or on local online news sites serving the area; (ii) inform customers that the reports will not be mailed (in the newspapers or by other approved means); and (iii) make reports available to the public upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication must target the area served; the system must actively inform customers that mailing will not occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception for very small systems (<=500) on publication/informing
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 500 or fewer persons may forego the publication and informing requirements if they provide notice that the report is available upon request at least once per year to their customers by mail, door-to-door delivery or by posting in one or more locations where persons served by the system can reasonably be expected to see it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual notice (at least once per year) must clearly state that the report is available upon request and be delivered via mail, hand delivery, or public posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record retention of CCRs (3 years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any system subject to this subpart must retain copies of its Consumer Confidence Report for no less than 3 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retention period begins from date of report; maintain copies to demonstrate compliance and for inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: LEP assistance plan requirement for systems serving >=100,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems serving 100,000 or more persons must develop a plan for providing assistance to consumers with limited English proficiency (LEP). The system must evaluate the languages spoken by persons with LEP served by the water system, and the system's anticipated approach to address translation needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First plan must be provided to the state with the first report in 2027; plans must be evaluated annually, updated as necessary, and reported with the certification required when submitting the CCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual distribution timing (July 1) and data year
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system must distribute reports by July 1 each year. Each report distributed by July 1 must use data collected during, or prior to, the previous calendar year using methods described in paragraph (a) of this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports cover the previous calendar year's data (or earlier) and must be distributed to customers by July 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biannual distribution requirement for systems >=10,000
rubrics_metrics.description: Each community water system serving 10,000 or more persons must distribute the report biannually, or twice per calendar year, by December 31 using methods described in paragraph (a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two distributions per calendar year are required, with the second distribution by December 31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Six-month update requirement when specified conditions occur
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to distribute biannually that have a violation or action level exceedance occurring between January 1 and June 30 of the current year, or have received monitoring results from required UCMR monitoring, must include a 6-month update with the second report including specified content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions triggering a 6-month update include MCL/MRDL/treatment technique violations, action level exceedances, or newly received UCMR results for samples collected during the reporting year but not included in the July 1 report.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-month update content for MCL/MRDL/treatment technique violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system receives an MCL, MRDL, or treatment technique violation, the 6-month update must include the applicable contaminant section information in § 141.153(d)(4), and a readily understandable explanation of the violation including: the length of the violation, the potential adverse health effects, actions taken by the system to address the violation, and timeframe the system expects to complete those actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To describe potential health effects, the system must use the relevant language of Appendix A to this subpart; include contamination-specific information per §141.153(d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-month update content for other violations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system receives any other violation, the 6-month update must include the information required by § 141.153(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §141.153(f) for the specific disclosure elements for non-MCL/MRDL/treatment technique violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-month update content for lead action level exceedance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a system exceeded the lead action level following monitoring conducted between January 1 and June 30 of the current year, the system must include information identified in § 141.153(d)(4)(vi) and (d)(8) in the 6-month update.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include lead-specific required information per referenced subsections (e.g., health effects, steps to reduce exposure).

rubrics_metrics.name: 6-month update content for late UCMR results
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring under § 141.40 that become aware of results for samples collected during the reporting year but were not included in the reports distributed by July 1, the system must include information as required by § 141.153(d)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include UCMR results and any required explanation/notification elements per §141.153(d)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report summary must be prominently displayed at the beginning
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report must include a summary displayed prominently at the beginning of the report, including a brief description of the nature of the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary serves as the lead section of the CCR and should concisely describe the report's purpose and key items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary minimum content: violations summary and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must include, at a minimum, the following information in the summary: (1) Summary of violations and compliance information included in the report required by § 141.153(d)(6) and (8), (f), and (h)(6) and (7). (2) Contact information for owner, operator, or designee of the community water system as a source of additional information concerning the report, per § 141.153(h)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include concise summaries of any violations and clear contact details for follow-up questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary must include directions for requesting a paper copy if certain delivery methods used
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable (for systems using delivery methods in § 141.155(a)(1)(ii), (iii), or (iv)), the summary must include directions for consumers to request a paper copy of the report, as described in § 141.155(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear instructions (how and where) for consumers to obtain paper copies when the system relies on non-mail delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary must include information on where to obtain translated copies/assistance for LEP consumers
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems subject to § 141.153(h)(3) because they serve a large proportion of consumers with limited English proficiency, the summary must include information where consumers may obtain a translated copy of the report, or get assistance in the appropriate language(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List contact points or links for translated CCRs or language assistance resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary must indicate when CCR also serves as public notification and how to locate notices
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems using the report to also meet the public notification requirements of subpart Q, the summary must specify that it is also serving to provide public notification of one or more violations or situations, provide a brief statement about the nature of the notice(s), and a brief description of how to locate the notice(s) in the report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label CCR sections that double as public notifications and provide navigation directions for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary style requirements: plain language; may use infographics
rubrics_metrics.description: The summary should be written in plain language and may use infographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use easily understandable wording and visual aids to increase consumer comprehension; for 6-month updates include brief description noting availability of new information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include standard language encouraging distribution to all persons served
rubrics_metrics.description: The report summary must include specified standard language encouraging the distribution of the report to all persons served (e.g., 'Please share this information with anyone who drinks this water ... You can do this by posting this report in a public place or distributing copies by hand, mail, email, or another method.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the required standardized wording verbatim to prompt secondary distribution to people who may not have received the report directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A: Regulated contaminants — required content and health-effects language
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix A lists regulated contaminants (microbiological, radioactive, inorganic, synthetic organic, volatile organic, PFAS/Hazard Index, etc.) with units, traditional MCLs, conversion notes for CCR, MCL in CCR units, MCLGs, major sources in drinking water, and recommended health effects language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When describing potential health effects for violations, systems must use the relevant language from Appendix A. Appendix A entries provide contaminant-specific MCL/MCLG/action level/MRDL values, major sources, and standard health-effects phrasing to be used in CCRs (e.g., lead: 'There is no safe level of lead in drinking water...' and PFAS hazard index language). Appendix A also defines unit abbreviations and key terms (AL, MCL, MCLG, MRDL, MRDLG, NTU, ppb, ppt, ppq, pCi/l, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart P applicability: enhanced filtration and disinfection for systems >=10,000
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations in Subpart P establish additional national primary drinking water regulations for filtration and disinfection applicable to subpart H systems serving at least 10,000 people, including treatment technique requirements (in lieu of MCLs) for Giardia lamblia, viruses, heterotrophic plate count bacteria, Legionella, Cryptosporidium, and turbidity. Each applicable system must provide treatment of its source water that complies with these treatment technique requirements in addition to those in § 141.70.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart P requirements became applicable beginning January 1, 2002 unless otherwise specified. Systems serving ≥10,000 must implement filtration/disinfection treatment techniques for the listed contaminants as national primary drinking water regulations.
